text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Forex dealers, panicky from speculation that dual exchange rate of naira will be merged and fixed at 56 naira to the dollar in 1997, offload their stock of foreign currencies.
- New umbrella body may be formed next year to replace manufacturers association and federation of chambers of commerce, industries, agriculture and mines.
- Volume of imports through Lagos port between January and November 1996 fell by 51 percent from same year-ago period.
- New laws may come into effect in 1997 pegging the maximum equity by any investor in an insurance company at 25 percent.

- Nigeria's stock market is under pressure from at least 18 institutional foreign investors to supply substantial number of shares which they can buy; market capitalisation at the moment is small and can be swallowed up by one major investor.
- National electoral commission set to register 52.7 million voters for next elections.
- It is unlikely that 1997 budget will be broadcast on New Year's Day when it is due, official sources say.
- Central Bank is seeking more powers to become autonomous in implementing monetary policy in line with the growing deregulation of the Nigerian economy, banking sources say.
- Central Bank sold a total of $1.861 billion at autonomous foreign exchange market in 1996, breakdown shows.
- Federal government may reduce company income tax in 1997 budget as part of incentives to boost manufacturing sector.
